extracted.intended_audience: media researchers, journalists, policymakers, and others interested in measuring and analyzing U.S. news media audience, circulation, revenue, and digital metrics
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, measurement rules, caveats, and thresholds used to calculate and report audience, circulation, revenue, and digital metrics for news outlets (TV, radio, print, and digital) in the Pew Research Center 'State of the News Media' analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viewership measurement (quarter-hour average)
rubrics_metrics.description: Viewership corresponds to the average of quarter-hour audience per time slot for all market affiliates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for reporting average viewership of TV news programs (source: Nielsen Media Research, used under license). Applies when comparing program audiences across years and affiliates; examples in tables and charts use this measure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-slot definitions for TV news categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Morning news: 5-7 a.m.; Early evening news: 5-7 p.m.; Late night news: 11-11:30 p.m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These fixed time definitions are used to classify affiliate program viewership into consistent categories across markets and years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percent-change comparisons across reporting periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Percent change is reported between comparable reporting periods (typically 2014 to 2015), but changes in reporting windows can affect comparability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: AAM moved from six-month publisher statements to quarterly reporting after March 31, 2015, so year-to-year comparisons may reflect different period lengths; the report flags when comparisons reflect different underlying periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large gain/loss threshold (10% rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: A large loss or gain represents at least a 10% difference between 2014 and 2015.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used when classifying site-level changes in unique visitors or minutes-per-visit (e.g., 'a large gain or loss represents at least a 10% difference between 2014 and 2015'). Sites without trendable data were omitted from these analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total Digital Population definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Total Digital Population is the unduplicated combination of the desktop (web browsing + video) and mobile traffic figures (websites and associated apps).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This unduplicated metric is used as the basis for digital audience comparisons; complete URL entities are used when available to map traffic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of comScore Media Matrix / Metrix for digital metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Digital unique visitors and minutes per visit are measured using comScore Media Matrix Multi-Platform and Desktop only, comparing Oct.-Dec. 2014 to Oct.-Dec. 2015.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data include desktop and mobile traffic (websites and, where available, associated mobile apps). Pew analysts worked with comScore to identify and remove web entities whose traffic shifts were measurement artifacts rather than organic changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital single copy sales: 'digital issue' category (AAM)
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies categorized as 'digital issue' typically feature the same advertising and editorial content as the print edition, although the content may be augmented with hyperlinks or additional media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This AAM-audited category is included in publisher statements and is the basis for reporting digital single copy sales; some titles also report a separate 'digital nonreplica' category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital nonreplica definition
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Digital nonreplica' generally represents editorial and advertising served on paywalled sites and apps and has been shortened or fundamentally altered to better suit the digital platform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the sample discussed, only The Economist and The Nation report digital nonreplica circulation; it is tracked separately from 'digital issue' in AAM data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting digital single copy sales from all-access programs (AAM 2014 test)
rubrics_metrics.description: Starting with 2014 data, AAM began counting digital copies from all-access programs as single copy sales (under a test period); these copies were only counted if a reader paid for the program and then requested or 'favorited' a specific magazine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This accounting change can materially affect year-over-year digital single copy sales (often inflating them), and for many titles the vast majority of digital single copy sales come from all-access programs (e.g., over 95% for some titles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Total circulation definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Total circulation is defined as the combination of single copy sales and subscriptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to report overall magazine circulation (print + digital single copy + subscriptions); single copy sales are emphasized as less affected by discount programs and thus a barometer of editorial appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of single-copy (newsstand) sales as editorial barometer
rubrics_metrics.description: Single-copy (newsstand) sales are an important barometer of a magazine's editorial appeal since they are not influenced by discount programs and promotions the way subscription circulation is.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pew emphasizes single-copy trends when assessing editorial appeal and year-to-year health of titles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital subscriptions reporting and caveats
rubrics_metrics.description: Digital subscription counts are reported (separately from digital single copy sales) but remain a small share of overall subscriptions and are affected by how app subscribers are counted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Growth in digital subscriptions may reflect changes in app counting, publishers' distribution strategies, or platform changes rather than purely organic subscriber growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling and cohort selection for niche digital media (Maynard Institute list)
rubrics_metrics.description: To analyze African American-oriented digital publishers, Pew used the Maynard Institute's list of African American-oriented sites and then queried comScore for detailed data; the Maynard list is not exhaustive but is an established accounting of key stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pew removed entities whose apparent traffic shifts were due to changes in measurement rather than organic audience changes; inclusion required trendable comScore data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform-specific behavior reporting (mobile vs desktop)
rubrics_metrics.description: When comparing desktop and mobile traffic, analyses consider both unique visitors and minutes per visit separately for each platform; mobile often shows higher unique visitors while desktop visits are longer on average.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports present results for desktop and mobile individually and note differing trends (e.g., many sites saw mobile unique visitor gains but declines in mobile minutes per visit).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data-source attribution and licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: Key data sources include Nielsen Media Research (TV viewership), Alliance for Audited Media (AAM) for circulation/audited publisher statements, comScore for digital audience metrics, and BIA/Kelsey for station revenue estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report cites licensing and auditing constraints (e.g., Nielsen data used under license) and notes when company-level disclosures limit network-specific revenue analysis (e.g., Telemundo).

rubrics_metrics.name: Revenue category definitions and caveats
rubrics_metrics.description: Revenue is reported by category where available (e.g., 'Total Revenue', 'Media Networks' including television and digital, and 'Radio'); some companies stopped reporting breakdowns by platform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparisons may be affected by one-time events (e.g., FIFA World Cup boosting 2014 revenue) and by companies ceasing to report platform-level revenue (e.g., Univision no longer reports total revenue by television or digital).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of non-trendable or incomplete data
rubrics_metrics.description: Sites or titles without trendable data for the comparison period are omitted from analyses of change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note example: five sites that did not have trendable comScore data for Q4-Q4 2014-2015 were omitted; authors flag omissions and provide notes on data availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of audited reporting windows and transition effects
rubrics_metrics.description: AAM's transition from six-month publisher statements to quarterly reporting after March 31, 2015 affects comparability of circulation figures between 2014 and 2015.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pew flags where differences in AAM reporting windows could influence year-over-year percentage changes (for example, Philadelphia Tribune summer circulation affected by school session months).
